# The `eco` command line

Every command of `eco`, with its arguments and flags. This page is generated:
`mise run cli:gen` writes it with `usage generate md` from the usage spec that
`eco usage` prints from the command definitions, and `mise run check` fails
when it no longer matches the binary. To change a line here, change the
command's definition in `src/main.rs` and run `mise run cli:gen`.

The commands reach eco in three ways.

- `setup` and `bench` run on their own. They need no daemon.
- `start`, `stop`, `restart` and `status` manage the daemon. `start` starts the
  `eco.service` user unit through `systemctl --user` when nothing answers on the
  socket, waits for the socket, and opens the window unless `--headless`. `stop`
  asks the daemon over the socket to stop and waits until it has. They print one
  line of plain text, such as `eco: daemon stopped`; `status` exits 3 when the
  daemon is not running.
- Every other command talks to the running daemon over its socket,
  `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/eco.sock`, and prints one JSON object on one line:
  `{"ok": true, "data": …}`, or `{"ok": false, "code": …, "message": …}` with
  exit code 1. With no daemon the code is `daemon.offline`. `export` is the one
  exception: it prints the WebVTT document itself, to pipe or redirect.

Agents use the same commands through the `eco` skill (`skills/eco/SKILL.md`).
Commands the user service and the daemon run for themselves are hidden from the
help, and so from this page.

---

## `eco`

Voice sessions with an AI beside them, for Omarchy


- **Usage**: `eco <SUBCOMMAND>`

## `eco setup`

- **Usage**: `eco setup [--harnesses… <HARNESSES>]`

Download the models, load the Hyprland rules and keep the agent skill current

### Flags

#### `--harnesses… <HARNESSES>`

Also publish the `eco` skill to these agent harnesses: agents, claude-code

- **Usage**: `eco start [--headless]`

- **Usage**: `eco stop`

- **Usage**: `eco restart`

## `eco bench`

- **Usage**: `eco bench <SUBCOMMAND>`

## `eco bench llm`

- **Usage**: `eco bench llm`

Time to first token of candidate models on OpenRouter (needs OPENROUTER_API_KEY)

## `eco bench diarization`

- **Usage**: `eco bench diarization [FLAGS] <DIR>`

Diarization error rate over recordings with reference RTTMs

### Arguments

#### `<DIR>`

Directory of `<name>.wav` (16 kHz mono) with `<name>.rttm` and optional `<name>.uem`

### Flags

#### `--list <LIST>`

File naming the recordings to run, one per line

#### `--model <MODEL>`

Speaker embedding model (ONNX); the one `eco setup` downloads by default

#### `--threshold… <THRESHOLD>`

Clustering thresholds to compare, e.g. 0.5,0.6,0.7

**Default:** `0.65`

#### `--min-share <MIN_SHARE>`

Smallest share of the speech a speaker may hold

**Default:** `0.02`

#### `--collar <COLLAR>`

Seconds forgiven around reference boundaries, half on each side

**Default:** `0`

#### `--output <OUTPUT>`

Directory to write eco's turns to as `<name>.rttm` (first threshold)

## `eco bench people`

- **Usage**: `eco bench people [--series… <SERIES>] <DIR>`

How safely people are named by voice across AMI meeting series

### Arguments

#### `<DIR>`

Directory of AMI `<series><a–d>.wav` with their `.rttm`

### Flags

#### `--series… <SERIES>`

Series whose meetings a–d hold the same people

**Default:** `ES2004,IS1009,TS3003,EN2002`

## `eco sessions`

- **Usage**: `eco sessions [FLAGS]`

List stored sessions, newest first, as JSON

### Flags

#### `--kind <KIND>`

Only sessions of this kind

#### `--person <PERSON>`

Only sessions linked to this person id

#### `--tag <TAG>`

#### `--search <SEARCH>`

Only sessions whose title, tags, lines, notes or answers hold this text (any case or accents)

## `eco import`

- **Usage**: `eco import [FLAGS] <PATH>`

Import an audio or video file into a new session

### Arguments

#### `<PATH>`

### Flags

#### `--title <TITLE>`

#### `--kind <KIND>`

#### `--language <LANGUAGE>`

#### `--participant <PARTICIPANT>`

Who the file is heard as; the user by default

#### `--date <DATE>`

When the recording began, local time: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS]. By default the date the file was recorded with, else when it last changed

#### `--no-wait`

Return once the import starts instead of when it ends
